texts.orig: Let k be a non-trivially valued non-Archimedean field. We consider a good, strictly k -analytic space X . We refer to 2.5 for the definition of PL functions. Recall from the introduction that an R -PL function u : X → R is called semipositive at x ∈ X if the associated residue line bundle Lu ( x ) ∈ Pic ( red ( X , x )) R is nef, where we refer to [ GJR21, 6.16-6.19 ] for residue line bundles. Equivalently, there is a strictly affinoid neighbourhood U of x such that u = h L for a formal k ◦ -model ( U , L ) of ( U , /Ocal U ) with L nef [ GJR21, Proposition 7.1 ] .

texts.orig: We will show first that for an R -PL function on a smooth curve, semipositivity is the same as subharmonicity in the sense of Thuillier's thesis [ Thu05, Définition 3.1.5 ] . Recall that Thuillier defines a subharmonic function on a smooth k -analytic curve X as a semicontinuous function u : X → R ∪ {-∞} which is not identically -∞ on any connected component of X and which has the property that for every harmonic function h on a strictly affinoid domain U of X with u | ∂ U ≤ h | ∂ U , we have u | U ≤ h .

texts.text: Proposition 5.1. Let X be a smooth, strictly k-analytic curve and let u : X → R be an R -PL function. Then u is subharmonic at x ∈ X in the sense of Thuillier if and only if L u ( x ) is nef.

texts.orig: Proof. First we treat the case when k is algebraically closed. As explained in 2.5, there exists a compact strictly analytic neighborhood U of x in X , a formal k ◦ -model U of U , and a formal model L of /Ocal U such that u | U = h L . Since k is algebraically closed, we may assume that the special fiber U s is reduced, which implies that U is covered by formal affines of the form Spf ( /Acal ◦ ) for a strictly k -affinoid algebra /Acal [ GJR21, §2.4 ] . It follows from [ Ber90, Proposition 2.4.4 ] that for every irreducible component Y of U s , there is a unique point ξ Y ∈ U reducing to the generic point of Y . In the formalism of real valued forms and currents on Berkovich spaces [ CD12 ] , it is well known that d ′ d ′′ [ u ] | U is the discrete measure on U supported on the points ξ Y of U for Y an irreducible component of U s , with multiplicity at ξ Y equal to deg L ( Y ) . See [ CD12, §6.9 ] for a more general statement. Wanner showed that subharmonicity of u on U is equivalent to the positivity of the current d ′ d ′′ [ u ] : see [ Wan19, Theorems 1 and 2 ] and use the fact that X is locally algebraic [ vdP80 ] . Thus L s is nef if and only if u is subharmonic on U . Suppose that u is subharmonic at x . Shrinking U , we may assume that u is subharmonic on U . This implies that L s is nef, so it follows from [ GJR21, Proposition 7.1 ] that Lu ( x ) is nef. Conversely, if Lu ( x ) is nef, then by [ GJR21, Proposition 7.1 ] , we may shrink U so that L s is nef, which as above implies that u is subharmonic on U .

texts.orig: It remains to show that subharmonicity of u at x and numerical effectivity of Lu ( x ) can be checked after extending scalars to the completion of an algebraic closure K = ( k ) ∧ . By [ GJR21, Proposition 7.6(2) ] , one can check that Lh ( x ) is nef after base change to K . The same is true for subharmonicity: this follows directly from Thuillier's definition and the fact that the base change of a harmonic function remains harmonic [ Thu05, Proposition 2.3.18 ] . □
